claims.text: NiTi shape memory alloys exhibit temperature-dependent plastic deformation behavior.
The temperature-dependent deformation transition in NiTi is caused by the martensitic-to-austenitic phase transformation.
Conventionally processed NiTi has a martensitic structure at lower temperatures.
Increasing temperature through the transformation range changes NiTi from martensite to austenite.
The phase composition and microstructure of NiTi change between martensitic and austenitic states.
At lower temperatures, martensite controls the deformation behavior of NiTi.
The low-temperature deformation of martensitic NiTi is characterized by stress-induced twinning.
Dislocation-based plasticity dominates after NiTi transforms to austenite at higher temperature.
The change from twinning-controlled martensitic deformation to dislocation-based austenitic plasticity produces different plastic deformation characteristics.
Increasing temperature will produce an observable change in yield strength or strain-hardening rate.
A notable change in deformation behavior will occur near the martensitic-to-austenitic transformation temperatures.
Variations in NiTi composition can alter its temperature-dependent deformation behavior.
Variations in processing history can alter the temperature-dependent deformation behavior of NiTi.
The transformation temperatures and quantitative mechanical-property changes depend on the specific NiTi composition and processing history.
